routing_reason: Existing Stripe Billing source update: full new raw + matched prior raw + current source; preserve version, UI variant, client/server, state and dated evidence boundaries; no semantic assumptions from collection diff alone.
findings: The core feature remains payment-gated subscription updates for invoice-generating changes, using payment_behavior=pending_if_incomplete on subscription or subscription-item update APIs, with charge_automatically and a listed supported payment method (new 9-13, 26-32, 34-63; old 8-12, 25-29, 60). The November text says this is normal behavior, then expressly excepts a matching pending update on paused-subscription resumption to active or past_due even if payment fails (new 28).

The November page corrects the May claim that a populated pending_update proves payment failure: it proves the update has not applied yet, while Payment Records may still process the reported payment; check invoice outcome (new 93-104 versus old 102-113). For Payment Records, invoice paid and subscription application may finish in separate requests; pending_update_applied is the confirmation for dependent provisioning (new 102).

New 15-24 qualifies add_invoice_items and distinguishes classic versus flexible billing with always_invoice. A standalone non-invoicing change applies immediately without pending_update or payment attempt, while pre-existing pending invoice items are a separate object (new 20-24). The new supported-attribute list includes metadata, discount fields, cancel_at_period_end and item discounts (new 118-147); appearing in that list does not mean every standalone field change creates an invoice or pending update.

New 106 suspends pending_invoice_item_interval invoices while a pending_update exists. New 159-161 expands automatic void/removal triggers to later updates carrying anchor, nonempty items, trial fields, or conflicting discount/cancellation changes, with discount ID and order rules; the existing summary lists only thresholds and schedule transitions (source 69).

New 183-188 distinguishes existing pending invoice item inclusion by flexible/classic mode and pending_if_incomplete. Metered usage discard and flexible removal qualification remain from old 177-181 and new 177-181. The corrected expires_at spelling in new 153 aligns with the example at new 81-83; old prose had expired_at at 156, and the 23-hour or earlier trial/item-period boundary otherwise remains.
substantive_changes: Add the paused-subscription resumption exception to payment-gated application (new 28); qualify the blanket payment-success-only source 13, 26 and concept 10, 14.

Replace the May inference pending_update means failed payment and immediate same-request application with the November not-yet-applied/Payment Records timing and pending_update_applied event boundary (new 74, 95, 102; old 83, 104, 111; source 45, 51; concept 34-35).

Refine no-invoice examples and supported-attribute claims: add_invoice_items differs across classic and flexible billing and context; metadata, discount and cancellation fields appear as supported attributes but do not independently prove invoicing (new 15-24, 118-147; source 21, 61).
Add interval-invoice suspension, later-update conflict/auto-void rules, and billing-mode-specific existing pending invoice item inclusion (new 106, 155-161, 183-188).
conflicts: Source 13, 26 and concept 10, 14 state payment success as an absolute gate, contradicted by the explicit paused-subscription resumption exception at new 28.

Source 45, 51 and concept 34-35 imply a pending_update indicates a failed payment and that paid invoice/application are immediate; new 74, 95, 102 require distinguishing pending processing from failure and waiting for pending_update_applied when using Payment Records.

Source 21 says add_invoice_items never generates an invoice, whereas new 20 makes that conditional on other invoice-triggering changes and billing mode; source 61 and concept 62 say metadata/config/discount attributes are unsupported, whereas new 118-147 lists metadata and discount attributes for specified endpoints.

Source 69 and concept 70 list only threshold and schedule phase as auto-void causes, omitting new later-update and discount/cancellation conflict triggers at 159-161. Source 82 / concept 83 keep a valid metered-usage warning but should not be read as covering existing pending invoice items, now detailed at 183-188.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the May 13 Node.js example and its supported-method snapshot as dated historical evidence (old 29-81); November's cURL example at 65-72 is a rendering/example change, not proof Node.js support was removed.

Preserve unchanged core behavior: charge_automatically and listed method prerequisite, original expiry on repeat failure, void-invoice cancellation, replacement invoice on changing pending values, 23-hour/earlier period-end expiration, schedule/threshold auto-void, metered usage caveats and Customer versus customer-configured Account event identity (old 29-60, 113-119, 152-181; new 32-63, 104, 108-112, 149-181).

Keep May's broad no-invoice metadata/discount examples and expired_at wording attributable to its capture only; new 118-147 uses these names in a supported-attributes list and new 153 says expires_at. Do not infer that listing alone changes standalone trigger behavior.
unresolved_questions: The new capture lists supported attributes alongside a principle that pending updates require invoicing; it does not show every combination's behavior, so do not claim metadata, discount or cancellation-only changes independently enter pending_update.

The Payment Records qualification establishes possible asynchronous application, not a universal delay or evidence of any particular reported payment outcome; verify invoice and pending_update_applied in an implementation.
The snapshot is dated November 7 and its payment-method list is a documentation eligibility list, not evidence that an account or customer can use every listed method.
